title: You didn’t feel it when it happened.
paragraphs: You didn’t feel it when it happened.

There was no thunder.
No voice from heaven.
No sudden collapse.
Saul still looked like a king.

He still wore the crown.
Still gave orders.
Still stood in front of the people like nothing had changed.
“Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul…” — 1 Samuel 16:14
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
The Spirit didn’t leave Saul suddenly.
It left him gradually, through every moment he chose disobedience over surrender.

A sacrifice he wasn’t authorized to give.
Impatience dressed up as leadership.
“You have done foolishly… your kingdom shall not continue.” — 1 Samuel 13:13–14

God said destroy everything.
Saul kept the best.

He renamed rebellion as wisdom.
Compromise as strategy.

“Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings… as in obeying the voice of the LORD?”
“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice…” — 1 Samuel 15:22

He said the right words.
Blamed the people.
Justified the disobedience.
But heaven doesn’t respond to performance.
“Because you have rejected the word of the LORD, He has also rejected you from being king.” — 1 Samuel 15:23
Saul asks for honor in front of the people.
But as a consequence already set in motion.

You can keep functioning
while being spiritually abandoned.

You can still lead, speak, post, smile—
while heaven is silent over your life.
You’re not struggling because God is absent.
You’re struggling because you’ve grown comfortable with partial obedience.

You call it “not that bad.”
God calls it rebellion.
But here’s the tension before truth:
what hope is there for you?
Because where Saul lost the kingdom through disobedience…
Jesus secured it through perfect obedience.
Where Saul spared what God said destroy…
Jesus destroyed what was killing you—sin itself.

“For as by the one man’s disobedience the many were made sinners,
so by the one man’s obedience the many will be made righteous.” — Romans 5:19
Saul tried to hold onto power.

“Create in me a clean heart, O God…
and take not Your Holy Spirit from me.” — Psalm 51:10–11

A man who failed—yes.
But repented.

Saul resisted correction.
David ran toward it.
You’re standing in that same place right now.
Keep leading your life like nothing’s wrong.

You can fall before God
and finally tell the truth.
Because the Spirit doesn’t remain where God’s voice is continually rejected.

Turn from the sin you’ve been justifying.
Surrender fully to Jesus Christ.
Because through Jesus, what Saul lost—
If this exposed something in you, don’t ignore it.
